summary: Pick one subplan. Language and Literature: the Latin or Greek syntax sequence, the second-language course, and 45 units with at least 25 numbered 200 and above. Classical Archaeology: CLASSICS 331 with a B or better, 15 graduate units in classical archaeology with a B or better, and 45 units with at least 25 numbered 200 and above. Ancient History: 20 units of graduate CLASSICS courses, 10 graduate units in other programs and 15 units of Greek or Latin at the 100 level or higher, with at least 30 units numbered 200 and above. No course below the 100 level counts toward the 45 units. You check by hand the Greek or Latin translation exam, the thesis or its equivalent, the modern language reading exam, the Program Proposal, and which courses are in classical archaeology or Greek and Latin.
